reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern is a quasi-periodic oscillation with a robust period of ~183 points, evident across all candidates. Each cycle consists of a sharp, near-symmetric rise (≈40–50 points) to a rounded peak (robust standardized value ≈3.5–4.2), followed by a slower, slightly asymmetric decay (≈100–120 points) through a shallow trough near −1.0 before rising again. Baseline level is stable around median 0.1–0.3 (robust standardized), with no strong long-term trend; slope per point is near-zero (±0.001), confirming stationarity at the cycle scale. Amplitude (90th percentile range) is consistently ~4.6–4.8, indicating high signal-to-noise. Peaks are smooth and unimodal, without shoulders or splitting; troughs are broad and gently curved, never sharp or flat-bottomed. Noise is low: roughness (~0.032) and curvature (~0.015) are tightly clustered, suggesting minimal high-frequency jitter. Boundary truncation is present in candidate 0 (single-cycle excerpt), but morphology matches the first cycle of longer candidates. Acceptable variation includes minor peak height fluctuations (±0.2), slight asymmetry in decay slope, and small baseline drift (<0.1 median shift) across windows—none disrupt the core motif.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer candidate 1 or 2 for query matching when ≥3 cycles are available—they provide the clearest consensus morphology with highest reliability. Use candidate 0 only for single-cycle queries or when aligning phase/initial conditions. Candidate 3 is best for assessing long-term stability or detecting subtle drift anomalies over >3 cycles. For queries with distorted peaks or asymmetric troughs, compare against candidate 1/2 as primary norm; if query matches candidate 0’s single-cycle shape but deviates in peak sharpness, treat as anomalous.
